free_tier.stated: 0.5 GB of data storage on a shared cluster with three-node replication, one free cluster per project, free forever

per_object_cap.stated: 16 mebibytes per BSON document, which is the MongoDB engine limit and not a tier limit

retention.stated: paused automatically after 30 days with zero connections; resumable unless the cluster ran a version Atlas can no longer restore to

egress.terms: 10 GB in and 10 GB out per rolling seven-day period; exceeding it throttles the cluster and adds a one-second cooldown per connection

interface_detail: the MongoDB wire protocol; a Data API for HTTPS access; the Atlas Administration API and the atlas CLI
tooling: mongosh, any MongoDB driver, the atlas CLI
chaining: a free document store that survives inactivity for a month, which is the longest idle clock in this class short of Aiven

limits.value: 100 operations per second, enforced by throttling with a one-second cooldown
0.5 GB of data storage; storage size is not configurable on a free cluster
10 GB in and 10 GB out per rolling 7-day period
paused after 30 days with zero connections

limits_note: 500 connections maximum; replication factor 3; no sharding, no network peering, and only a subset of regions

identity_cost.detail: an Atlas account; no card on Free

reliability_note: the page is explicit that Atlas may deactivate idle free clusters under its terms, and recommends exporting a copy before a long pause
confidence_note: both pages were read today: the Atlas free-tier limits page for the 0.5 GB, the pause and the throttles, and the server limits page for the 16 mebibyte document cap. the page states 0.5 GB.

evidence.proved: 'Free clusters: 0.5 GB' for Data Storage; 'Atlas automatically pauses Free clusters after 30 days of inactivity where there are zero connections'; 10 GB in and out per rolling seven-day period; 100 operations per second; 500 connections; 'You can't configure storage size for Free clusters'
'The maximum BSON document size is 16 mebibytes', which is an engine limit and not an Atlas tier limit

notes: 0.5 GB is a hard wall rather than an overage, and 100 ops/s is a throughput cap that no storage allowance can exceed. The 30-day idle clock is the most forgiving in this class and it is still a clock.
